docs.title: INDstocks API (Skopaq reference)
docs.text:
Skopaq's notes on the INDstocks REST endpoints it calls: the request and response shapes it relies on, how it reads order statuses and fills, where the official documentation contradicts itself, and what still has to be checked against the live API.

The canonical documentation is https://api-docs.indstocks.com/ (a single-file export is at https://api-docs.indstocks.com/llms-full.md, the OpenAPI spec at https://api-docs.indstocks.com/openapi-spec.yaml). If this page disagrees with it, the official docs win: fix the code and this page. This page was written from the September 2026 export ("Docs last updated: unknown").

The client is skopaq/broker/client.py (INDstocksClient); status and row parsing live in skopaq/broker/order_status.py; live order handling in skopaq/execution/live_orders.py.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://api.indstocks.com (SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_BASE_URL).
  • Auth header: Authorization: <token>, with no Bearer prefix. A token lasts 24 hours: skopaq token set <TOKEN> every trading day, or automatically from TOTP (POST /generate/token with the Client ID as x-api-key, MPIN and the current code; skopaq token auto, skopaq/broker/auto_token.py). Each TOTP generation invalidates the previous TOTP token; one a minute; 5 wrong codes lock generation for 15 minutes.
  • Instruments are addressed by scrip code, {EXCH}_{SECURITY_ID} (for example NSE_2885 for RELIANCE). Market data takes scrip-codes=NSE_2885, never symbols=NSE:RELIANCE. Orders take the bare security_id (2885).
  • Static IP: placing, modifying and cancelling orders needs a whitelisted IP: two slots, IPv4 or IPv6, each changeable once a calendar week (NSE circular NSE/INVG/67858). SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_STATIC_IPS tells Skopaq which they are (skopaq preflight).
  • Algo id: every order carries algo_id: 99999 on NSE, 9999999999999999 on BSE (SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_ALGO_ID_NSE / _BSE for registered ids).
  • Profile: GET /user/profile also answers ucc, is_nse_onboarded, is_nse_fno_onboarded, is_bse_fno_onboarded and is_ddpi_active, which the readiness check reads. Read-only calls (quotes, historical data, order book, profile, funds) do not, so confirming a fill works from anywhere; placing does not.
  • Timestamps: historical data takes epoch milliseconds and returns candle ts in epoch seconds. Order rows carry ISO-8601 times with a +05:30 offset.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Category Limit Covers Order APIs 10/s; at most 25 modifications per order place, modify, cancel Non-Trading APIs 15/s, 100,000/day profile, funds, order history (order book, GET /order, trades) Quote APIs 5/s, 100,000/day quotes, LTP Data APIs 5/s, 100,000/day instruments, historical data, option chain Token generation 1/min

Going over returns HTTP 429. Each client keeps its Non-Trading reads (order book, GET /order, trades, trade book, positions, holdings, funds, profile) to 12 in any rolling second, so a burst of live SELLs (each reads the book, positions, holdings and funds before it is placed) is not refused. Quotes and data calls (instruments, history, option chain) are held to 4 in any rolling second each, and order calls to 8 (also under SEBI's 10 orders a second for unregistered retail algos). A 429 on a GET is retried twice after a pause (Retry-After, else 1 s, 2 s); an order is never re-sent. The live order worker stays well inside them: by default it polls each order once a second, and all the orders it is watching share one order-book read (0.5 s cache).

docs.title: Response envelope
docs.text:
• Success: {"status": "success", "data": ...}. Historical data uses {"success": true, "data": ...}.
  • Errors normally come with HTTP 4xx/5xx and {"status": "error", "message": ..., "error_type": ...} (the conventions page shows error_code instead). Other shapes occur: {"message": ..., "success": false}, {"message": "Bad Request", "debug_info": ...} and {"error": "Rate limit exceeded", "success": false}.
  • A 2xx can carry a failure body, for example {"status": "failure", "error": {"msg": ...}}. On POST /order that has been seen for an order that was placed.

Skopaq reads market data leniently (_request: unwrap data if present) and every order and portfolio call strictly (_request_envelope):

  • a 2xx body with status error/failure, success: false, or a non-empty error, error_type or error_code raises BrokerError(kind="error_body"), so a failure is never read as "no orders" or "no positions";
  • data: null is accepted (as empty) only under status: success or success: true;
  • a 2xx body that is not JSON, or a list endpoint answering something that is not a list, raises BrokerError(kind="bad_payload").

BrokerError.kind says how far a request got:

Kind Meaning An order sent this way… not_sent never left the host (client not open, expired token, connect error or timeout) was not placed http the broker answered HTTP ≥ 400 4xx: was rejected; 5xx: may exist transport read/write error or timeout after sending, connection dropped may exist bad_payload 2xx that is not JSON or not the expected shape may exist error_body 2xx whose body reports a failure may exist

place_order raises OrderPlacementUncertain whenever the order may exist (and when a 2xx answer has no order id). The worker then looks for it in the order book by order ids that were not there before the placement, and never sends it again blind.

docs.title: Market data
docs.text:
Endpoint Client method Request Response (data) GET /market/quotes/full get_quote, get_quotes scrip-codes=NSE_2885,NSE_11536 dict keyed by scrip code: live_price, day_open, day_high, day_low, prev_close, day_change, day_change_percentage, volume, best_bid_price, best_ask_price GET /market/quotes/ltp get_ltp scrip-codes=NSE_2885 {"NSE_2885": {"live_price": 1362}} GET /market/historical/{interval} get_historical scrip-codes, start_time and end_time in epoch ms; interval such as 1minute, 5minute, 1day {"NSE_2885": {"candles": [{"ts", "o", "h", "l", "c", "v"}]}}, ts in epoch seconds GET /market/instruments get_instruments source=equity, fno or index CSV (not JSON): SECURITY_ID, TRADING_SYMBOL, CUSTOM_SYMBOL, EXCH, SEGMENT, INSTRUMENT_NAME, LOT_UNITS, EXPIRY_DATE, STRIKE_PRICE, OPTION_TYPE, TICK_SIZE, SYMBOL_NAME; index is three columns, EXCH,SEGMENT,SECURITY_ID, the second holding the index name

skopaq/broker/scrip_resolver.py caches the instruments CSV for an hour: resolve_scrip_code gives the scrip code, resolve_tick_size the TICK_SIZE.

docs.title: Derivatives (F&O)
docs.text:
Endpoint Client method Request Response (data) GET /market/option-chain get_option_chain exchange (NSE/BSE), segment of the underlying (INDEX/EQUITY), underlying-scrip (the underlying's SECURITY_ID, never a contract's), expiry (YYYY-MM-DD), strike_count (per side; 2n + 1 strikes) underlying_ltp, expiry, strikes: an object keyed by strike (sorted by Skopaq), each with ce / pe legs: security_id, trading_symbol, last_price, oi, previous_oi, volume, top bid/ask, iv (percent), greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega). No lot size or other expiries GET /market/instruments/expiries get_expiries underlying, segment=DERIVATIVE ascending list of upcoming YYYY-MM-DD GET /market/instruments/search search_derivatives underlying, segment=DERIVATIVE; optional instrument_type (OPTIDX, OPTSTK, FUTIDX, FUTSTK), expiry, option_type, strike_from, strike_to, page, page_size (≤ 100) count, instruments: security_id, trading_symbol, expiry, strike_price / option_type (null for futures), lot_size GET /margin get_margin JSON body on the GET, all strings: segment, exchange, securityID, txnType, quantity, price, product total_margin, span_margin, exposure_margin, insufficient_balance, …, charges (stt, brokerage, gst, total_charges, …) GET /portfolio/positions get_derivative_positions segment=derivative, product=margin / intraday as the equity rows; kept apart from get_positions because derivative security ids are another numbering

skopaq/broker/fno.py maps names to ids: resolve_underlying (NIFTY → NSE INDEX 40000001 from the index file; RELIANCE → its cash-market id), expiry_at, lot_size (cached an hour), find_option, nearest_future. skopaq/options/chain.py builds the chain (fetch_option_chain) from these.

Derivative orders: segment=DERIVATIVE, product MARGIN (carry forward, "NRML") or INTRADAY, qty in units (a whole number of lots: OrderRequest refuses anything else, and CNC on a derivative), the contract's security_id. Order ids start DRV-. The derivatives endpoints answer a malformed date with the same 400 as an unknown underlying, so the client checks YYYY-MM-DD first.

docs.title: Orders
docs.text:
Endpoint Client method Request Response (data) POST /order place_order JSON: txn_type (BUY/SELL), exchange, segment (EQUITY), product (CNC/INTRADAY/MARGIN), order_type (LIMIT/MARKET), validity (DAY), security_id, qty (int), limit_price (not for MARKET), is_amo, algo_id; remarks only with SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_ORDER_REMARKS_ENABLED=true {"order_id": "EQ-93586788", "order_status": "INITIATED"} POST /order/modify modify_order JSON: order_id, segment, qty, limit_price (all four mandatory) {"order_id", "order_status": "MODIFIED"} POST /order/cancel cancel_order JSON: order_id, segment {"order_id", "order_status": "CANCELLED"} GET /order get_order order_id, segment as a JSON body on the GET; Skopaq sends the same as query params too one order row GET /order-book get_order_book — list of order rows; null (under status: success) when there are none GET /order/trades get_trades order_id, segment as a JSON body on the GET (and query params) fills: fill_id, exch_order_id, quantity, price, trade_date GET /trades/{order_id} get_trades (fallback) — fills (older docs; different field names, quantity and price in both) GET /trade-book get_trade_book segment=EQUITY (required) today's fills, one row each: fill_id, exch_order_id, quantity, price, trade_date, trade_serial_no, scrip_code, remarks (if sent); no order id and no side: join on exch_order_id

Notes:

  • POST /order only acknowledges the order. The status key is order_status, not status. Validation and RMS rejections come back at once as HTTP 400 (below); whether the order fills is decided at the exchange afterwards. skopaq/execution/live_orders.py confirms every live fill by reading the order back.
  • Order ids: EQ-… (equity), DRV-… (derivatives), GTT-… (smart orders). The id POST /order returns is the order row's id and what GET /order, cancel and trades take.
  • A cancel races the order filling: always re-read the order afterwards; the final status can be SUCCESS or PARTIALLY FILLED - CANCELLED. Position could not be found. means the order does not exist or has already completed; The order is already pending… means try again shortly. Stop and GTT orders are cancelled on /smart/order/cancel, which Skopaq does not use.
  • Skopaq never modifies an order: a resting exit is cancelled and the rest re-placed.
  • Skopaq also sends trigger_price on POST /order when the order has one. It is not a documented field there (stops exist only on /smart/order); whether it is ignored or refused is unverified.

docs.title: Portfolio and account
docs.text:
Endpoint Client method Request Response (data) GET /portfolio/positions get_positions segment=equity and product=cnc / product=intraday, both required, lowercase flat list: position_id, security_id, symbol, segment, product, exchange, isin, net_qty, avg_price, buy_qty, buy_avg, sell_qty, sell_avg, realized_profit, day_buy_qty, day_buy_val, day_sell_qty, day_sell_val, cf_* (the day_* and cf_* values can be null) GET /portfolio/holdings get_holdings — security_id, symbol, isin, total_qty (T1 + DP), used_qty, avg_price, t1_qty, t1_avg_price, dp_qty, dp_avg_price; no product, LTP or P&L GET /funds get_funds — detailed_avl_balance: eq_cnc (CNC buying power, Funds.available_cash), eq_mis, option_buy, option_sell, future (the *_available fields); pledge_received, … GET /user/profile get_profile — profile
  • Positions: seeing CNC and intraday rows takes two calls. Each row's product echoes the query, so Skopaq sets it from the query rather than trusting the row. If both queries are refused (400/404/422) it retries without parameters; a failed read always raises, it never becomes "no positions". A {"net_positions": [...]} wrapper is accepted. Null numbers read as 0.
  • Holdings: Holding.quantity is total_qty and Holding.average_price is avg_price. used_qty ("pledged, sold, or otherwise blocked") is kept as used_quantity but not subtracted, because a sale today is taken to show already as a negative CNC net_qty in positions (still to be verified, below).
  • Read the order book before positions and holdings (read_broker_snapshot in skopaq/broker/book_snapshot.py). An order that fills between the reads is then counted twice (still open in the book, already sold in positions), which understates what can be sold; the other order would count it zero times and allow a double sell.

docs.title: Order rows (GET /order, GET /order-book)
docs.text:
Field Notes id the order id (not order_id) exch_order_id exchange id; "" until the order reaches the exchange txn_type BUY / SELL security_id the instrument on that exchange: the same stock has another security id on BSE, so compare it only within one exchange isin the instrument across exchanges ("" for derivatives); positions and holdings carry it too, and Skopaq matches the same shares on NSE and BSE by it name display name (for example NIFTY 3 JUL 25700 CE): not a trading symbol, and rows have no trading symbol exchange, segment, product, validity, mkt_type, off_mkt_flag as sent order_type a MARKET order keeps MARKET after INDstocks turns it into a LIMIT requested_qty, traded_qty integers; traded_qty is the quantity filled so far requested_price string; for a MARKET order the limit it was converted to traded_price string, "" until something fills; read as the average fill price (the docs do not say) sl_trigger_price, sl_limit_price, tgt_trigger_price, tgt_limit_price strings, "" on regular orders status see the table below extra_info rejection reason or exchange message; empty for pending or successful orders remarks only if sent at placement created_at, updated_at ISO-8601 with +05:30

There is no remaining-quantity or average-price field: remaining is requested_qty − traded_qty. Parse rows with parse_order_row / parse_order_book from skopaq.broker.order_status (they accept a few alternate key names, never use name as the symbol, and drop only rows without an id); never compare raw status strings.

docs.title: Order statuses
docs.text:
The 15 documented statuses, and how skopaq.broker.order_status.classify reads each when the quantities say nothing more:

Status Skopaq state Documented meaning QUEUED working queued for processing O-PENDING working after-market order pending (also returned for ordinary placements) SL-PENDING working stop-loss pending trigger PROCESSING working being processed INITIATED working initiated and sent to the exchange MODIFIED working successfully modified PENDING working pending execution at the exchange PARTIALLY FILLED working partly executed, rest still working SUCCESS filled fully executed PARTIALLY FILLED - CANCELLED partial partly executed, rest cancelled (with traded_qty 0 or missing: fill unknown, never "nothing") PARTIALLY FILLED - EXPIRED partial partly executed, rest expired (the same) CANCELLED cancelled cancelled by the user or the system EXPIRED cancelled expired without execution FAILED rejected failed (technical or other reasons) ABORTED rejected aborted (system or validation issues)
  • There is no REST status called REJECTED, COMPLETE, OPEN or TRIGGER PENDING: rejections show as FAILED or ABORTED. Those names, PARTIALLY_EXECUTED, PF-CANCELLED/PFC, PF-EXPIRED and RJ are still accepted as aliases, and case, underscores and dash spacing are normalised.
  • Quantities overrule the status: traded_qty ≥ requested_qty > 0 is filled whatever the status says, and a no-fill final status with traded_qty > 0 is partial.
  • A status in none of these lists is unrecognised: treated as still working until the timeout (then cancelled and re-read) and logged once per order. SKOPAQ_ORDER_EXTRA_TERMINAL_STATUSES declares extra statuses final without a deploy.
  • The filled quantity is unknown, not 0, when a partial or working status comes without traded_qty. A protective exit then stops with a CRITICAL alert instead of re-selling.

The order-updates WebSocket uses short codes (R, P, S, F, C, RJ, PF, PFC). Skopaq confirms fills by polling REST; the feed is only printed by skopaq ticks --orders (see WebSockets below).

docs.title: WebSockets
docs.text:
skopaq/broker/websocket.py (PriceFeed, OrderUpdateFeed):

Feed URL Subscribe Frames Prices wss://ws-prices.indstocks.com/api/v1/ws/prices (SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_WS_PRICE_URL) {"action": "subscribe", "mode": "ltp", "instruments": ["NSE:2885"]}, batches of 50 {"mode": "ltp", "instrument": "2885", "timestamp": <ms>, "data": {"ltp": 1426}} Orders wss://ws-order-updates.indstocks.com/api/v1/ws/trades (SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_WS_ORDER_URL) {"action": "subscribe", "mode": "order_update"} a JSON string holding the update (decoded twice): order_id, order_type (side), order_status (short code), executed_price, lot, req_quantity
  • Auth: Authorization: <token> on the handshake, no Bearer. Without a valid token the server refuses the handshake (seen: HTTP 513).
  • Instruments are SEGMENT:TOKEN (NSE:, BSE:, NFO:, BFO:, NIDX:, BIDX:): REST scrip codes with : for _. A tick names the token without its segment, so it is matched to the subscription with that token; a token subscribed on two segments is dropped as ambiguous.
  • Heartbeats and frames Skopaq does not understand are ignored. Both feeds reconnect with backoff (1 s doubling to 60 s) and re-subscribe.
  • Order updates are kept per order id, newest envelope timestamp first.

The position monitor uses the price feed when SKOPAQ_WS_PRICE_FEED_ENABLED (default on): a tick younger than SKOPAQ_WS_TICK_MAX_AGE_SECONDS replaces a REST quote, and its rules run every SKOPAQ_MONITOR_TICK_POLL_SECONDS. Without a fresh tick it asks GET /market/quotes/ltp, at most once per SKOPAQ_MONITOR_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS per position. skopaq ticks RELIANCE prints the live ticks with 1-minute candles and indicators (skopaq/market/candles.py): check the feed with it before relying on it.

docs.title: Fills
docs.text:
• Filled quantity: the larger of traded_qty and the sum of the order's trade quantities, capped at requested_qty.
  • Average price, in this order: the volume-weighted average of the order's trades (Σ quantity × price / Σ quantity) when they add up to the filled quantity; traded_price; the trade book's fills joined on exch_order_id; the average of whatever trades were found; else Skopaq's reference price (fill_price_source="estimate", with a WARNING).
  • Skopaq books ₹10 brokerage per order that filled (INDstocks' flat API fee, INDSTOCKS_BROKERAGE_PER_ORDER_INR; GST comes on top). get_margin gives the exact charges of one order.

docs.title: MARKET orders and tick size
docs.text:
"API trading does not support pure MARKET orders": INDstocks converts a MARKET order to a LIMIT at the live price before it reaches the exchange, so it can rest unfilled in a falling market. RMS can also refuse it outright ("Market orders are blocked for this instrument."). Skopaq therefore cancels a resting protective exit and re-places the rest as a LIMIT a little below the LTP, rounded down to the tick:

  • the tick is the instruments CSV TICK_SIZE when it is plausible (above 0 and at most 0.2 % of the price; its unit is not documented);
  • otherwise a coarse tick valid in every NSE price band: 0.05 below ₹1,000, 1.00 below ₹20,000, 5.00 above.

A LIMIT refused for its price (tick, circuit, price band) is retried as MARKET in the same attempt; "Market orders are blocked" makes the next attempt a LIMIT.

docs.title: Synchronous rejections
docs.text: POST /order answers HTTP 400 for validation failures (DayValidityAllowed, QtyWithinFreezeQty, PriceWithinRange, …) and RMS rejections, with a free-text message: RMS: Margin exceeds …, Market orders are blocked for this instrument., tick size, circuit. classify_rejection sorts them into rate_limited (429), price, market_blocked, auth (401/403, token), not_sent and other. A protective exit backs off on rate_limited and not_sent (1, 2, 4, 8 s, at most 15 s per exit) without using an attempt, and stops with a CRITICAL alert on auth and other.

docs.title: Where the official docs disagree
docs.text: Topic The docs What Skopaq does GET /order request a JSON body on a GET; no example with query params sends both; falls back to the order-book row; sticks to whichever source answered Per-order fills Orders page and OpenAPI: GET /order/trades with a JSON body; API overview and older docs: GET /trades/{order_id} tries /order/trades, falls back on 404/405 for that call; a path becomes the preference only after it returned a fill Positions segment and product required and lowercase, flat array; older pages show a net_positions / day_positions wrapper and no parameters two queries (cnc, intraday); the call without parameters if both are refused; the wrapper accepted validity the enum is DAY, IOC, but the validations say "Order should be placed with DAY validity" always DAY; resting re-placements are cancelled by Skopaq instead O-PENDING described as an after-market order pending also returned for ordinary placements: treated as working traded_price not defined read as the average fill price; the trades' VWAP is preferred remarks listed under "[Unreleased]" in the changelog sent only when SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_ORDER_REMARKS_ENABLED=true Rate limits the conventions table (above) vs "10 orders/s, 100 API calls/s" in the v1.0.0 changelog follows the table for polling Holdings total_qty / avg_price now; an older page showed quantity / average_price accepts both

docs.title: To verify live
docs.text:
None of this has been checked against the live API yet (tests/integration/test_indstocks.py covers the token and market data only). Check it by hand with 1 share from the whitelisted host, or as new -m integration tests, and record the answers here:

  1. A 1-share LIMIT BUY far below the market: the status while it rests, then cancel it and read CANCELLED; the real status strings and row keys (id, updated_at, product).
  2. Which GET /order form works (JSON body or query), which trades path works, and the trades fields.
  3. /portfolio/positions with and without parameters; the equity CNC row after a same-day BUY and SELL (sell_qty, day_sell_qty, net_qty).
  4. Holdings vs positions for T1 shares (no double counting); whether selling earlier holdings today shows a negative CNC net_qty; total_qty / used_qty before and after.
  5. How soon positions reflect a filled SELL (this sets SKOPAQ_ORDER_SELL_FILL_LAG_WINDOW_SECONDS).
  6. Whether validity=IOC on POST /order is accepted.
  7. The unit of TICK_SIZE in the instruments CSV (rupees or paise) for a ₹200, ₹2,000 and ₹6,000 stock.
  8. A MARKET SELL's row: does order_type stay MARKET, and is requested_price the converted price?
  9. The answer to cancelling a completed order (Position could not be found.) and to a cancel while "already pending".
  10. Whether remarks is accepted and echoed in the order book.

docs.title: Adaptive AI (FreqAI-style)
docs.text: skopaq/adaptive/ brings FreqAI's ideas to Indian equities, implemented natively. Freqtrade (and FreqAI) is GPL-3.0, while this project is Apache-2.0, so no Freqtrade code is copied. FreqAI is also tied to Freqtrade's crypto exchange layer.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
FreqAI idea Here Feature expansion across timeframes, periods, shifts and correlated pairs features.FeatureExpander (details below). Values use only bars closed at the decision time Outlier detection: Dissimilarity Index, SVM/DBSCAN outliers.DissimilarityIndex on live points. filter_training (robust z-score, optional Isolation Forest) on the training rows Many model libraries LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost and the NumPy logistic baseline (--model). Saved as text/JSON, never pickle Periodic live retraining adaptive_auto_retrain: retrains at the end of a session after adaptive_retrain_hours (see "Where it differs") Backtesting that emulates retraining engine.rolling_backtest: trains on the last train_days, predicts the next retrain_days, repeats. Every prediction is out of sample Hyperopt hyperopt.hyperopt (Optuna TPE, fixed seed) for the scalper's strategy parameters Reinforcement learning PPO, A2C and DQN (rl_agents.py, PyTorch) in an environment that replays the scalper's own rules net of charges (rl_env.py). A policy trades as the rl_policy scalp strategy behind every gate (rl_live.py, see below). rl.py stays a tabular research baseline

FeatureExpander builds, for each timeframe (1, 5 and 15 minutes) and each period:

  • RSI, ROC, ATR %, Bollinger width, distance from the SMA, relative volume;
  • ADX, DI and the EMA 9/21 gap;
  • RSI and ROC shifted by 1–3 bars;
  • the same set for each correlated symbol;
  • session minute and day of the week.

docs.title: Your own strategy (full control)
docs.text:
Subclass skopaq.adaptive.strategy.AdaptiveStrategy. These hooks match FreqAI's:

  • feature_engineering_expand_all(df, period, metadata) — runs once per timeframe and period;
  • feature_engineering_expand_basic(df, metadata) — once per timeframe;
  • feature_engineering_standard(df, metadata) — once, on the base timeframe;
  • set_targets(df, metadata) — sets the targets;
  • entry_signal(prediction, metadata) (optional) — decides an entry from the prediction.

Naming: features start with % and targets with &. Set model_type = "regressor" to predict values instead of classes. A full example is in examples/adaptive_strategy_example.py. Use your class with --strategy file.py:Class or SKOPAQ_ADAPTIVE_STRATEGY (set in .env only, because it runs code).

Higher timeframes are resampled from the base bars and joined only once they have closed. Shifted copies and the correlated symbols' features are added automatically.

Look-ahead guard. Features are recomputed with the history cut at several points. If any earlier value changes (for example shift(-1) or a centred window), training is refused. FreqAI has no such check.

docs.title: Data pipeline
docs.text:
skopaq/adaptive/pipeline.py is fitted on the training rows only. The steps, in order:

  1. Variance threshold.
  2. Scaler: minmax (FreqAI's default), standard, robust or none.
  3. PCA (99.9 % of variance).
  4. Outlier detectors, each optional:
  5. One-class SVM — removes training outliers and flags live points;
  6. Dissimilarity Index;
  7. DBSCAN — removes training noise and flags live points far from every core point.
  8. Training noise.

weight_factor weights recent rows more, using FreqAI's formula. All fitted parameters are stored as JSON. The SVM and DBSCAN checks are re-implemented in NumPy from the stored support and core points.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
kind library task saved as lightgbm LightGBM classifier / regressor, early stopping lightgbm.txt xgboost, xgboost_rf XGBoost both, early stopping xgboost.json catboost CatBoost both, early stopping catboost.cbm random_forest, extra_trees scikit-learn both trees.npz (arrays, no pickle) linear NumPy logistic / ridge linear.json mlp, ft_transformer PyTorch both, early stopping torch.safetensors

Each target gets its own model (multi-target).

docs.title: Prediction output
docs.text:
Each prediction returns:

  • Per target:
  • value;
  • training label_mean / label_std;
  • pred_mean / pred_std, taken from the last 500 live predictions once there are 20, otherwise from validation (like FreqAI's fit_live_predictions);
  • zscore.
  • Data check: do_predict (1 ok, 0 outlier, -1 not enough data) and the missing_features count.
  • Outliers: the di value and each detector's flag (detectors).
  • Entry: entry, plus the entry_rule used: a probability threshold or mean + k·std, chosen on validation, or the strategy's entry_signal. Backtests and live use the same rule.
  • Model: version, age_hours, top_features.

The scalper's signals store this output in evidence.adaptive. With the model gate on, a bundle decides with its own entry rule.

docs.title: Model saving
docs.text:
Each model is saved as a bundle in <model_dir>/artifacts/<version>/:

  • the model files;
  • pipeline.json.gz;
  • bundle.json, which holds the strategy layout, features, targets, statistics, entry rule and feature importance;
  • report.json;
  • manifest.json, which holds the SHA-256 and size of every file, the library and Python versions, and the training data fingerprint.

On load, every file is checked against its hash, and any change refuses the model. The commands:

  • skopaq model-verify — checks all bundles;
  • skopaq model-export VERSION file.tar.gz and skopaq model-import file.tar.gz — move a bundle between hosts. The import refuses .. paths and links, and lands as a candidate that is gated again;
  • SKOPAQ_ADAPTIVE_KEEP_MODELS — retention. The champion, shadow and rollback target are never deleted.

Install the optional libraries:

  • pip install -e ".[ml]" — LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Optuna, scikit-learn;
  • .[torch] — PyTorch, using the CPU wheels.

docs.title: Where it differs from FreqAI, deliberately
docs.text:
FreqAI uses a retrained model at once. Here a retrained model is only a candidate:

  1. Gates on unseen data. Before a model may move on, it must pass all of these on the test period:
  2. at least 100 test samples;
  3. at least 30 gated trades;
  4. beat the baseline and the current champion;
  5. profit factor ≥ 1.1;
  6. a 90 % confidence interval of expectancy above zero;
  7. a drawdown no worse than the baseline's;
  8. a better Brier score than the base rate.
  9. Shadow. A model that passes is recorded on every signal but never decides.
  10. Champion. It is promoted only after the shadow days and a named admin's approval.

Rollback restores the previous champion.

  • The gate is opt-in. The champion's probability and Dissimilarity Index are recorded on every signal (evidence.adaptive). They decide entries only with SKOPAQ_*_MODEL_GATE_ENABLED and SKOPAQ_BLOCK_MODEL_OUTLIERS.
  • Labels are net of costs. The forward target asks whether a fixed-notional long over horizon_bars makes money after Indian charges and slippage, not merely whether the price rises.
  • Hyperopt needs approval. Parameters are searched on 70 % of the days and must beat the current ones on the other 30 %. Only then can an admin approve them, and rollback is supported. Risk limits are never part of the search.

docs.title: Your strategy without code (dashboard)
docs.text:
AI learning → Your strategy (admin) builds a strategy from fixed lists, saved as JSON in <model_dir>/strategies/ (skopaq/adaptive/spec.py):

  • Timeframes: 1m base plus up to three of 3m–1h. Periods: up to four (2–200). Shifted copies: 0–5. Correlated symbols: up to five.
  • Features: rsi, roc, atr_pct, bb_width, sma_dist, ema_dist, zscore, rel_vol, stoch_k, willr, cci (per period), pct_change, ema_gap, macd_hist, body, close_pos, vwap_dist, minute_of_session, day_of_week. Every one looks backwards only.
  • Targets (1–4): win (classifier: beats min_move_pct after horizon bars), forward_return, max_up, max_down (regressors).
  • Entry rule: auto (the threshold validated in training), probability ≥, zscore ≥ or value ≥.

The server validates every field and runs the look-ahead guard before saving; nothing in a spec is executed as code. Use selects what training learns (a saved spec, the .env code strategy or the built-in default), logged with who and why. skopaq adaptive-train --strategy my_spec (or spec.json) trains it directly. A bundle stores its spec, so live predictions rebuild the same strategy without any .env setting. A model trained on it is a candidate like any other.

docs.title: Continual learning
docs.text:
FreqAI's continual_learning: SKOPAQ_ADAPTIVE_CONTINUAL_LEARNING=true or adaptive-train --continual. A run continues the previous model of the same strategy and model kind (champion, else shadow, else the newest bundle), instead of starting from scratch:

Model Continued by LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost adding trees to the previous ensemble (init_model / xgb_model) MLP / transformer starting from the previous weights logistic / ridge starting from the previous coefficients random / extra-trees forest, XGBoost RF cannot be continued: trained afresh

The parent's fitted pipeline (scaler, PCA, detectors) is kept frozen, so the continued model keeps the input space it learned. Other features, targets or task mean a fresh fit, with the reason in report["continual"]. The rolling backtest chains its retrains the same way. The bundle records its parent (shown on the dashboard).

RL: SKOPAQ_RL_CONTINUAL_LEARNING=true or rl-train --continual continues the previous policy of the same algorithm and network size (weights and observation scaling); DQN starts with less exploration. In both cases the result is still a candidate behind the gates, the shadow period and an admin's approval.

docs.title: Reinforcement learning: PPO, A2C, DQN
docs.text:
FreqAI drives stable-baselines3; here the three algorithms are compact native PyTorch implementations (skopaq/adaptive/rl_agents.py), saved as safetensors + JSON with a SHA-256 manifest (no pickle).

Environment (rl_env.py): one session of 1-minute candles, decided on each close and filled at the next open with slippage. Actions: hold, enter long, exit (masked when they do not apply). Every entry gets the live geometry (ATR stop bounded 0.4–2.5 ATR, rr target) and is managed by the scalper's own update_trail / exit_reason (stop, trail, target, time stop) and the square-off time; the agent can only exit earlier. An entry the live scalper would refuse on cost (its reward-to-charges check, or net reward/risk after charges and slippage below SKOPAQ_SCALP_MIN_NET_RR) is not taken in training either. The reward is the change of equity after every charge, so the rewards of a day add up to its net P&L. Observations: 10 point-in-time features plus the position state.

Evaluation: trained on each symbol's earlier sessions, replayed greedily on its later unseen sessions; the report (net, profit factor, bootstrap CI, drawdown, charges, exits) goes through the registry's gates against a buy-and-hold baseline.

Live / paper trading (rl_live.py), opt in with SKOPAQ_RL_ENABLED=true and rl_policy in SKOPAQ_SCALP_STRATEGIES:

Policy used Paper account RL champion, else the shadow policy (SKOPAQ_RL_PAPER_USE_SHADOW) Live account the RL champion only (gates passed, shadow days, named admin approval) and SKOPAQ_RL_ALLOW_LIVE=true in .env (locked against dashboard overrides)

On a closed candle the policy's enter becomes a scalp Setup that passes the regime map, the cost check, SignalGate qualification (net R:R after charges, spread, liquidity, model gate), sizing, the entry gate and the safety checker (kill switch, limits, funds) like any other strategy; the decision and its action scores are journalled as evidence.rl. Its exit sells a position it opened through the normal exit path; it cannot move a stop or a target. RL registry: <model_dir>/rl (separate from the model gate's champion). Dashboard: AI learning → Reinforcement learning.

docs.title: Commands (no orders)
docs.text:
skopaq adaptive-train --symbols RELIANCE,TCS,INFY --correlated HDFCBANK --days 30 --model lightgbm
skopaq hyperopt --symbols RELIANCE,TCS --days 30 --trials 60
skopaq rl-research RELIANCE --days 30
skopaq rl-train --symbols RELIANCE,TCS --algo ppo --days 60      # or a2c / dqn
skopaq rl-status
skopaq rl-promote <version> --by "Your Name" --reason "7 paper days reviewed"
skopaq rl-rollback --by "Your Name" --reason "..."

To install the optional libraries: pip install -e ".[ml]" (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Optuna). Without them, training falls back to the logistic baseline.

The dashboard's AI learning → Adaptive AI card shows:

  • the configuration and the last retrain;
  • the latest model's test and rolling-retrain results (every bar vs model vs model with the outlier gate);
  • the hyperopt candidate, with its approve and roll-back buttons.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Results on synthetic data in the tests prove the mechanics, not an edge. Use real INDstocks history: the token is set in .env.
  • An RL policy learns from the same few weeks the gates test it on later; with little data PPO / A2C often learn "never trade" (charges dominate), which is the honest outcome.
  • Feature expansion costs a few milliseconds per bar: training on 30 days × 10 symbols takes minutes. The daemon's retrain has a 15-minute budget.

docs.title: Execution safety, signals and learning
docs.text: How a setup becomes a trade, and what stops it. This page also holds the audit's gap matrix and the current readiness status.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
ticks / REST → CandleBuilder (closed bars only)
  → market/quality.check_series      invalid, duplicate, out-of-order, missing, forming, stale
  → market/indicators + patterns     EMA/SMA/RSI/MACD/ADX/ATR/BB/ROC/RelVol, swings, S/R, ORB
  → market/regime + timeframes       trend/range/vol label; higher timeframe from completed buckets
  → strategy (scalping/strategies)   Setup: entry, stop, target, reason
  → strategy/signal.qualify          QUALIFIED / REJECTED / EXPIRED + reasons → signal journal
  → Executor ─ BUY: EntryGate (one entry at a time) + reconciliation blockers
             └ SafetyChecker         kill switch, limits, loss streak, funds, risk state
  → OrderRouter → LiveOrderWorker    write-ahead journal → place → confirm fill / reconcile
  → position management              stop, breakeven, trail, target, time stop, flatten
  → finance/charges + ledger         per-order charges, net P&L, slippage
  → signal journal outcome           → learning dataset → candidate → shadow → champion

Indicators, sizing, risk checks, order states and money are deterministic code. There is no LLM: the Adaptive AI's models (e.g. the swing model) only decide which qualified setups to take; they cannot set prices or skip any check below.

docs.title: Signal contract
docs.text:
skopaq/strategy/signal.py defines SignalCandidate. Its fields:

  • ids: signal, strategy and version, model version
  • instrument and product, direction, decision time, timeframe
  • entry, invalidation, stop and target; holding period
  • costs and slippage assumptions, expiry
  • evidence: indicators, patterns, regime, data quality, higher timeframe

qualify rejects a setup in these cases:

  • the data is stale, invalid or still forming;
  • the stop is on the wrong side, or too tight or too wide;
  • the regime is unreliable (when required), or a required higher-timeframe or pattern confirmation is missing;
  • net reward/risk, after round-trip charges and adverse slippage on both sides, is below SKOPAQ_SCALP_MIN_NET_RR.

The regime and higher-timeframe filters are off by default. No out-of-sample evidence supports them yet, so they are recorded as evidence only.

confidence is a rule-based confirmation score, not a win probability. A model's calibrated probability is stored separately as model_prob.

Every decision goes to ~/.skopaq/signals/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (SKOPAQ_SIGNAL_JOURNAL_DIR), together with its later execution and outcome lines. The dashboard shows them on Signals & risk.

docs.title: Sequential entries and reconciliation
docs.text:
skopaq/execution/entry_gate.py controls BUYs:

  • One entry at a time. A BUY holds the gate from the safety check until the broker's answer is final. Within a process this is an asyncio.Lock. Across processes on one host in live mode it is an flock on <SKOPAQ_ORDER_LOCK_DIR>/entry-account.lock.
  • Waiting is bounded. A second entry waits SKOPAQ_ENTRY_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS, then is refused.
  • The lock fails closed. In live mode, an unusable lock directory refuses entries.
  • Unknown outcomes block BUYs:
  • an uncertain BUY;
  • an own BUY still working;
  • a journalled submitting line with no answer. It is written before every placement, so a process killed mid-placement leaves evidence.

An admin resolves these from the dashboard after checking the broker's order book. The resolution is audited. - SELLs never take the gate. Protective exits keep running while entries are blocked.

The lock is per host. Two machines trading one account are not coordinated. Run one trading host per account.

Other changes in this area:

  • No paper fallback in live mode. A live order without a live client used to be filled on paper (the MCP server). It is now refused.
  • Risk state survives restarts. Today's losing streak (SKOPAQ_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_LOSSES, ceiling 4, can only be lowered) and the last loss time (cool-down) are seeded from stored trades.
  • Fail-closed risk state. In live mode, if Supabase is configured but cannot be read, new BUYs are refused.
  • Fail-closed kill switch. In live mode an unreadable system_flags row counts as a halt for BUYs (source supabase-unreadable), so a halt set from another machine is never missed. SKOPAQ_KILL_SWITCH_FAIL_OPEN=true (.env only) restores the old behaviour. The Supabase read has a 3 s timeout and the executor refreshes it off the event loop.
  • MARKET orders are value-checked. A MARKET order carries no price, so the order value cap, position size, sector concentration and funds checks use the signal's reference price (the LTP or entry it was built from). A BUY with no price at all is refused.
  • Weekends and NSE holidays. The market-hours check also refuses orders on weekends and on the calendar's NSE holidays plus SKOPAQ_NSE_HOLIDAYS.
  • Broker endpoints are locked. SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_BASE_URL, the WebSocket URLs, SKOPAQ_BINANCE_BASE_URL, SKOPAQ_SCHEDULER_PING_URL and SKOPAQ_UPSTASH_REDIS_URL cannot be changed from the dashboard: they receive the broker token, MPIN/TOTP or keys.
  • Net P&L for loss limits. The loss limits record P&L after estimated charges.

docs.title: Charges and net P&L
docs.text:
skopaq/finance/charges.py is one versioned schedule (nse-indstocks-2024-10). Each rate carries its effective date and source. It covers intraday and delivery equity, options and futures, and computes the net break-even exit.

  • GST is levied on brokerage + exchange + SEBI fees only.
  • Brokerage is per order, so partial fills are never charged twice. This fixes the scalper's partial exits, which used to re-charge the entry brokerage.
  • Components the schedule does not model are listed in excluded.

skopaq/finance/ledger.py builds P&L from confirmed fills only. It covers average prices, gross/unrealized/net P&L, slippage, broker-confirmed charges and discrepancies.

Not yet wired: contract-note charges are not fetched from the broker. Net P&L is labelled estimated until they are.

docs.title: Learning lifecycle
docs.text:
There are two separate things:

  • Statistical learning is learning/tracker.py and report.py.
  • Model training:
  • dataset.py builds point-in-time features from journal or backtest evidence. Labels are the net outcome; a missing outcome is unlabelled, never a loss.
  • check_point_in_time rejects leakage.
  • The split is chronological with an embargo; walk-forward folds are also run.
  • model.py is a deterministic NumPy logistic baseline.
  • evaluation.py measures, on the unseen test set:
    • net expectancy with a bootstrap CI;
    • profit factor;
    • drawdown;
    • Brier vs base rate and calibration;
    • drift (PSI).
  • registry.py moves a model from candidate → shadow (gates passed) → champion. Promotion needs mandatory_paper_days_for_new_strategy days in shadow plus a named admin approval. Rollback is supported, and history is kept.

assert_no_safety_keys refuses any artifact naming a SafetyRules field or a hard config limit.

To train a candidate (no orders; INDstocks token needed for candles):

skopaq learn-train --symbols RELIANCE,TCS --days 20 --journal

The swing book has its own registry (skopaq swing-train, skopaq/swing/model.py, same candidate → shadow → champion flow): its model does gate swing entries (paper: champion, else shadow; live: champion only; no model, no swing entries). For the scalper and F&O engine the champion's probability gates entries only with the model gate on (below).

docs.title: API hardening
docs.text:
• SKOPAQ_API_TOKEN, if set, is accepted as an admin bearer token (dashboard_auth.py); everyone else logs in through Supabase Auth.
  • Errors no longer echo exception text.
  • /api/status and /api/portfolio need a login; jobs, orders, model promotions and the kill switch need an admin.
  • In live mode, /docs is off by default. The API also refuses to start without dashboard auth, or with CORS=*.
  • The login lockout trusts only SKOPAQ_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS entries of X-Forwarded-For.
  • POST /control/orders and /control/close accept an Idempotency-Key (the dashboard sends one). An identical body within 5 s is refused. This state is per process.

docs.title: More execution safeguards
docs.text:
• Order lifecycle (skopaq/execution/order_lifecycle.py): 13 explicit states (CREATED, VALIDATED, SUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED, CANCEL_PENDING, CANCELLED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, FAILED, UNKNOWN, RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) and the allowed transitions between them.
  • Every step is journalled: the executor writes created/validated; the worker writes submitting, placed, cancel_sent, final, uncertain, stuck and not_placed.
  • The lifecycle is replayed from the journal. A transition the table does not allow is kept, because the broker is the truth, and flagged.
  • The dashboard shows it on Signals & risk.
  • Startup reconciliation (startup_reconcile.py). Before a live process's first BUY:
  • unresolved placements are matched against the order book: one candidate → reconciled (adopted); none → reconciled_absent; several → still blocking, CRITICAL alert;
  • external orders are reported;
  • an unreadable order book keeps entries blocked.
  • Cross-host leases (lease.py, SKOPAQ_ACCOUNT_LEASE_ENABLED, Upstash Redis):
  • an entry lease is held inside the host flock;
  • a daemon session lease makes a competing session on another host refuse to start, with a CRITICAL alert;
  • if Redis is enabled but unreachable, entries are refused.
  • Open losses count: unrealized losses (never gains) count toward the daily loss stop.
  • Alerts: each alert carries an incident id and the action to take:
  • entry blocked by reconciliation, risk state, daily/weekly/monthly lockout, loss streak or kill switch;
  • stale data;
  • competing session or a lost session lease;
  • external orders;
  • model drift.
  • Candles: a quiet instrument's candle is closed by a timer (CandleBuilder.flush). Duplicate ticks and late ticks for a closed candle are dropped.

docs.title: Strategy coverage
docs.text:
• Scalper: qualified per setup.
  • F&O engine: qualified on the premium, with option-specific stop bounds and spread.
  • Swing (Adaptive AI) book: BUYs are qualified on daily candles before the executor. The stop is the setup's ATR stop; the target is the configured SKOPAQ_MONITOR_TARGET_MODE target, or, when that gives none (off), the setup's R-multiple target (SKOPAQ_SWING_TARGET_RR, passed as the signal's agent_state["target_rr"]).

All three journal their decision, execution and outcome (swing: decision and execution). Spread and liquidity limits (SKOPAQ_SCALP_MAX_SPREAD_PCT, SKOPAQ_SCALP_MAX_PARTICIPATION) apply when quotes carry bid/ask and bars carry volume.

Regime-adaptive selection (strategy/selector.py):

  1. skopaq learn-train --regimes builds a regime → strategy map from held-out trades. A strategy is allowed only with at least 30 trades and a 90 % CI of net expectancy above zero.
  2. The map is used only after an admin approves it, and can be rolled back.
  3. With an approved map, a regime that no strategy covers means no trade.
  4. Without one, every configured strategy runs (the fallback).

Model gate: the champion's probability is recorded on every signal, and the shadow model's probability too. It decides entries only with SKOPAQ_*_MODEL_GATE_ENABLED=true. LightGBM is an optional candidate (--model lightgbm, pip install .[ml]); it is stored as text, never as a pickle.

Evolution: skopaq/backtest/evolve.py picks RSI parameters on the first 70 % of the history and adopts them only if they beat the current parameters on the last 30 %. Moves are limited by max_parameter_change_per_evolution_pct.

docs.text: skopaq/finance/reconcile.py imports the broker's contract-note CSV (INDstocks has no contract-note API) from the dashboard or with skopaq charges-reconcile. It compares it with the journal's estimates per day and symbol and saves the report. broker_quote reads GET /margin charges as broker-quoted figures (not confirmed ones).

docs.title: MCP Server Architecture
docs.text: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is how SkopaqTrader integrates with Claude Code and other AI assistants. It exposes 26 tools via the FastMCP framework over stdio transport. The tools read data, the Adaptive AI's swing ideas and the track record, run safety checks and backtests, and place paper orders; no tool calls an LLM.

docs.title: What Is MCP?
docs.text:
MCP is a protocol that allows AI assistants to call external tools. Instead of the AI writing Python code to access your broker, it calls structured MCP tools that handle authentication, error handling, and data formatting.

AI Assistant (Claude Code)
       │
       │  MCP Protocol (stdio)
       ▼
  skopaq/mcp_server.py
       │
       ├── Broker API (INDstocks)
       ├── Order router (paper engine) + SafetyChecker
       ├── Swing engine + swing model registry (Adaptive AI)
       ├── Data vendors (tradingagents/dataflows)
       └── Signal journal / trade history

docs.title: FastMCP Framework
docs.text:
The server uses FastMCP, a Python framework for building MCP servers. Tools are defined as decorated async functions:

from mcp.server import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP(
    name="SkopaqTrader",
    instructions="SkopaqTrader MCP server for Indian equity trading...",
)

@mcp.tool()
async def get_quote(symbol: str) -> str:
    """Get a real-time market quote for a stock symbol."""
    # ... implementation
    return json.dumps({"symbol": symbol, "ltp": 2485.50, ...})

Key design principles:

  • All tools are async -- They can call async broker APIs without blocking
  • All tools return JSON strings -- Structured data that Claude can parse
  • Lazy initialization -- Infrastructure (config, broker clients) is built on first tool call, not at import time

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
The server uses stdio transport -- it reads requests from stdin and writes responses to stdout. This is the default transport for Claude Code MCP servers.

// .claude/.mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "skopaq": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["-m", "skopaq.mcp_server"]
    }
  }
}

Claude Code launches the Python process and communicates with it over pipes. No network ports are needed.

docs.title: Lazy Infrastructure
docs.text:
To keep startup fast, the server uses lazy initialization:

_infra_cache: dict = {}

def _get_config():
    if "config" not in _infra_cache:
        from skopaq.config import SkopaqConfig
        _infra_cache["config"] = SkopaqConfig()
    return _infra_cache["config"]

At startup (python -m skopaq.mcp_server) the server applies the settings saved from the dashboard (skopaq.env_overrides.apply()), then waits on stdin. The first tool call that needs them builds:

  1. SkopaqConfig -- loads .env and validates all settings (_get_config())
  2. OrderRouter + PaperEngine -- paper trading infrastructure (_get_router())

The data tools (gather_*, backtest_strategy, run_monte_carlo_test) also call _setup_dataflow_config(), which sets the vendored tradingagents/dataflows config for route_to_vendor: INDstocks then yfinance for prices (yfinance only for crypto), yfinance for indicators, fundamentals and news, with the .NS suffix for NSE symbols. The swing tools build a SwingEngine from the config on each call.

Subsequent calls reuse cached objects.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
INDstocks is the only broker. Market data tools open an INDstocks client per call; portfolio and order tools go through the cached OrderRouter (paper engine):

@mcp.tool()
async def get_quote(symbol: str) -> str:
    async with INDstocksClient(config, TokenManager()) as client:
        scrip_code = await resolve_scrip_code(client, symbol)
        q = await client.get_quote(scrip_code, symbol=symbol)
    return json.dumps({...})

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All tools catch exceptions and return structured error JSON:

try:
    chain = await load_option_chain(symbol, expiry_index, config=_get_config())
    return json.dumps({...})
except Exception as exc:
    logger.exception("Option chain fetch failed")
    return json.dumps({"error": str(exc)})

This ensures Claude always gets a parseable response, even on failure.

For debugging, run the server directly:

It will start and wait for MCP messages on stdin. You can also run it inside Docker:

docs.text:
Sent by OrderAlerter (skopaq/execution/order_alerts.py) in the background, so placing or cancelling an order never waits for Telegram, and deduplicated by key within the process (a blocked exit retried every 10 seconds sends one message). An alert about particular orders ends with their broker order ids ("Orders: EQ-…").

Severity Examples CRITICAL exit-not-filled, exit-partial, exit-rejected, exit-replace-blocked, sell-refused (a protective exit, or the order book or holdings unreadable), exit-blocked, order-stuck, order-deadline, order-interrupted, placement-uncertain, placement-match (an order that only looks like a lost placement: watched, never cancelled), fill-qty-unknown (an exit), sell-without-book (at most once per symbol every 10 minutes), exit-late-unpriced, late-fill-unpriced, late-fill/exit-late of an order only matched by its look, booking-unconfirmed (a late fill's booking failed or never finished: its shares may not be booked — check trade rows), late-fill-unclaimed (a final late fill not booked: the journal directory is unwritable — book it by hand), positions-left (skopaq monitor: once a day for the same state) WARNING sell-refused (any other SELL), entry-partial, fill-qty-unknown (an entry), fill-price-unknown, late-fill, exit-late, position-dropped, partial-not-split, sell-not-booked, sell-lock-unavailable, journal-write-failed

docs.title: Chat Registration
docs.text:
Notifications are sent to all registered Telegram chat IDs. Registration happens when:

  1. User sends /start to the Telegram bot
  2. Code calls register_chat(chat_id)
  3. The default chat ID is set via SKOPAQ_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID

register_chat(123456789)        # Register a specific chat
set_default_chat(123456789)     # Set as default + register

If neither is set, notifications are logged to console only.

docs.title: How Telegram Delivery Works
docs.text:
async def notify(message: str) -> None:
    logger.info("NOTIFY: %s", message[:100])  # Always log

    chat_ids = _get_chat_ids()
    if not chat_ids:
        return  # No registered chats

    token = os.environ.get("SKOPAQ_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
    if not token:
        return  # No bot token

    bot = Bot(token)
    for chat_id in chat_ids:
        await bot.send_message(chat_id=chat_id, text=message)

Each notification creates a new Bot instance. Failed sends are logged but do not raise exceptions -- the trading system continues regardless of notification failures.

docs.title: Extending to New Channels
docs.text:
To add a new notification channel (e.g., Slack, email):

  1. Add the delivery logic inside notify()
  2. Add configuration variables to SkopaqConfig
  3. The event-specific functions (notify_trade_event, etc.) all call notify(), so they automatically get the new channel
async def notify(message: str) -> None:
    logger.info("NOTIFY: %s", message[:100])

    # Telegram
    await _send_telegram(message)

    # New: Slack
    await _send_slack(message)

docs.title: Trading Pipeline (Adaptive AI)
docs.text: SkopaqTrader has one decision-maker: the Adaptive AI — machine-learning models trained on our own market data, signals and trades. There is no LLM and no API AI anywhere in the trading path.

docs.title: The three books
docs.text:
Book Engine Decides with Command Swing (delivery, out the same day) skopaq/swing/engine.py daily setups + the swing model skopaq daemon, skopaq scan Intraday scalps skopaq/scalping/engine.py rule strategies, adaptive models, RL policies skopaq scalp F&O (options buying) skopaq/scalping/fno_engine.py index setups + adaptive models skopaq fno

All three send every entry through the same SignalGate (skopaq/strategy/gate.py) and the same Executor → SafetyChecker → OrderRouter.

docs.title: Swing book
docs.text:
PRE_OPEN   load the swing model (champion; on paper the shadow if there is no champion)
SCANNING   SwingEngine.scan(universe)
             for each symbol: a year of daily candles (today's forming bar dropped)
             → the setup on the last closed bar (trend_pullback / breakout / oversold_bounce)
             → point-in-time features → the model's P(win)
             → kept when P(win) ≥ the threshold chosen on validation data; best first
TRADING    SwingEngine.trade(idea)
             → SignalGate.decide: net reward/risk after delivery charges, data quality,
               stop distance 0.5–15 %, journalled QUALIFIED / REJECTED
             → Executor: ATR position sizing, regime and calendar scaling,
               SafetyChecker (kill switch, limits, funds), paper or live
             → exit plan: the setup's ATR stop and its R-multiple target
MONITORING PositionMonitor: stop, target (partial booking), trailing, EOD exit at 15:20
CLOSING    sells what is still held; REPORTING sends the session summary

Without a usable model the swing book makes no entries. SKOPAQ_SWING_RULES_ONLY=true lets a paper account trade the raw setups (ranked by trend strength) to collect a record; it is ignored on a live account.

docs.title: Setups
docs.text:
Rules on closed daily bars (skopaq/swing/setups.py); the first that fires wins:

Setup When trend_pullback close > SMA50 > SMA200, EMA20 > SMA50, a low within 1 % of EMA20, green bar above EMA20, RSI 40–65 breakout close above the 20-day high on > 1.5× average volume, closing in the top 30 % of the bar, above SMA50 oversold_bounce above SMA200, yesterday's RSI < 35, close above yesterday's high

Entry = the last close; stop = entry − SKOPAQ_ATR_MULTIPLIER × ATR(14); target = entry + SKOPAQ_SWING_TARGET_RR × risk.

docs.title: The swing model
docs.text:
skopaq/swing/model.py:

  1. Dataset — every historical bar where a setup fired, with its features (returns, RSI, ATR %, distance to the moving averages, SMA50 slope, volume ratio, range position, gap, the setup) and the outcome of trading it: buy at the next open plus slippage, stop first, then target, else out at that day's close — the same-day exit the live book makes — net of delivery charges.
  2. Split by date — train (60 %), validation (15 %: picks the probability threshold), test (the latest 25 %, never seen).
  3. Gates — the model becomes a shadow only if, on the test dates, it has enough samples and taken trades, beats taking every setup, has a profit factor ≥ 1.1, a 90 % expectancy CI above zero, no worse drawdown and a better Brier score. Otherwise it stays a candidate.
  4. Promotion — after the shadow period (SafetyRules, 7 days) an admin promotes it to champion (skopaq swing-promote, dashboard AI learning page). Live sessions trade only a champion. skopaq swing-rollback restores the previous one.

Bundles are pickle-free (the model library's own format, the pipeline as JSON, a SHA-256 manifest verified on every load); a tampered bundle is refused and the book makes no entries.

docs.title: What the AI cannot change
docs.text: SafetyRules (skopaq/constants.py), the loss limits, the kill switch, position and order caps, the stop on every BUY and paper-by-default are outside every model. Learning only decides which qualified setups to take.

docs.title: Claude Code Setup
docs.text: SkopaqTrader integrates with Claude Code via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Once connected, its 26 tools (broker data, portfolio, the Adaptive AI's swing ideas, safety checks, backtests, paper orders) are available inside your Claude Code session. The decisions come from the Adaptive AI; Claude Code reads and reports them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+ installed
  • SkopaqTrader cloned and dependencies installed (pip install -e .)
  • A .env file (copied from .env.example) with a valid INDstocks token, or one set with skopaq token set
  • For the swing ideas: a trained swing model (skopaq swing-train, see Swing Trading)

docs.title: Register the MCP Server
docs.text:
Option 1 — Project-level config (recommended):

Create or edit .claude/.mcp.json in your project root:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "skopaq": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["-m", "skopaq.mcp_server"]
    }
  }
}

Option 2 — Global config (available in all projects):

Edit ~/.claude.json and add the same block under "mcpServers".

Use absolute Python path

If Claude Code cannot find python3, use the full path: 

"command": "/usr/local/bin/python3"
Find yours with which python3.

docs.title: Verify the Connection
docs.text:
After saving the config, restart Claude Code and ask:

What is the current status of the SkopaqTrader system?

Claude calls mcp__skopaq__system_status and shows version, trading mode, asset class, token health, the swing model (champion and shadow versions), paper capital and the kill-switch state.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The MCP server (skopaq/mcp_server.py) runs as a child process using stdio transport. Claude Code launches it automatically and communicates over stdin/stdout. No network ports are needed.

Claude Code  ──stdin/stdout──  python -m skopaq.mcp_server
                                   │
                                   ├── INDstocks (quotes, candles, option chain)
                                   ├── Order router (paper engine) + SafetyChecker
                                   ├── Swing engine + swing model registry (Adaptive AI)
                                   └── Signal journal / trade history (reports, learning)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem Solution Tools not appearing Restart Claude Code after editing .mcp.json ModuleNotFoundError Run pip install -e . in the project root Broker errors Ensure a valid INDstocks token (skopaq token status, or SKOPAQ_INDSTOCKS_TOKEN in .env) Swing tools return model: null No swing model trained yet: run skopaq swing-train MCP server crashes Run python -m skopaq.mcp_server standalone to see errors

Environment Variables

The MCP server reads from your shell environment (and the settings saved from the dashboard). If you use direnv or a .env loader, make sure variables are exported before Claude Code launches.
